bull_case: Continued cash displacement, tokenization, Visa Direct and VAS can extend double-digit economics for years.
bear_case: Regulatory routing/interchange limits and alternative rails could reduce take rates or network relevance.
thesis: Visa combines secular digital-payment penetration with category leadership and multiple adjacent growth vectors. Regulation is persistent, but the network has repeatedly adapted while volume and services keep expanding.

evidence.claim: FY2025 nominal payments volume was $13.894T and processed transactions 257.545B.

counterevidence: Regulatory and interchange litigation can pressure network economics and pricing over time.
The current valuation already embeds a high-quality compounder profile.
unknowns: Long-run regulation of interchange and routing
Sustainable growth rate of Visa Direct and value-added services
falsifiers: If processed transactions and payments volume decelerate materially while client incentives rise faster than gross revenue, the moat/FCF thesis weakens.
next_checks: Payments volume, cross-border volume, processed transactions, value-added services, client incentives, owner FCF/share, buyback price

subscores.rationale: Digitization of payments and money movement is a multi-decade structural trend.
Visa is one of the global networks that defines acceptance, authorization and tokenization standards.
Consumer payments, cross-border, commercial/money movement and VAS create multiple independent growth/earnings buffers.

uncertainties.rationale: Regulation, incentives and valuation are the main uncertainty.
